Senses.Explanation: Inspect mind or look at mind. The compound is attested, but 257 hits are concentrated in the Record of the Source-Mirror, and the corpus does not give the action one uniform set of predicates. In the Daoxin–Niutou Farong encounter, Farong answers ‘inspecting mind’ when asked what he is doing; Daoxin asks, ‘Who is doing the inspecting, and what thing is mind?’ (觀是何人，心是何物), and Farong gives no answer. The Treatise on Breaking Appearances says, ‘Only inspecting mind, this one thing, gathers all things’ (唯觀心一法，總攝諸法), then asks, ‘How does inspecting mind count as understanding?’ (云何觀心稱之為了). Its reply distinguishes a clean mind and a soiled mind and later says, ‘Inspecting mind in this way may be called understanding’ (如是觀心可名為了). The Record of the Source-Mirror quotes a different direct formula: ‘Inspect mind as no mind; things do not dwell on things; my mind is itself empty; fault and fortune have no owner—this is called correct inspection’ (觀心無心，法不住法，我心自空，罪福無主，即是無心無數，名為正觀). Other Chan witnesses criticize particular uses. The Yongzheng Emperor says that making silence final and ‘then devoting oneself to quietly inspecting mind’ is ‘escaping a pit and falling into a ditch’ (便務靜觀心，又所謂逃坑落塹). Layman Xuri says, ‘closing the eyes, vainly seek seeing; inspecting mind, mistakenly seek penetration’ (閉目妄求見，觀心誤覓通). Zhang Tingyu, Layman Chenghuai, writes that ‘holding mind and inspecting mind divide guest and host’ (持心觀心紛主客). Chaoding Yuxuan writes, ‘if inspecting mind here is clear, the undivided single flavor is itself alert’ (於此觀心若了了，混然一味自惺惺). These are text-drawn assertions and criticisms by different named voices; they do not supply a single imported category for the headword.

Senses.Note: Two occurrences in one work count as one work, and no philosophical object-theory is added.

Recorded Sayings of Ancient Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄): Recorded Sayings of the Ancient Worthies (古尊宿語錄), complete Mayu–Linji exchange: after Mayu Baoche asks which face of twelve-faced Guanyin is correct, Linji Yixuan takes the sitting mat and asks where twelve-faced Guanyin has gone.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰。觀音妙智力。能救世間苦。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X80/X80n1565.xml). Five Lamps Compendium (五燈會元): Five Lamps Compendium (五燈會元), Guizong Zhichang section: Guizong quotes ‘Guanyin's wondrous power of wisdom can save the world's suffering’; when the monk asks what that power is, Guizong strikes the cauldron lid three times.

Senses.Explanation: Guanyin is the invoked figure whom the records place in images, questions, manifestations, named gates, and public exchanges. Fachang Yiyu makes an ink-painted Guanyin operate a mill; the unnamed questioner asks Lingyin Qingsong for Guanyin's first principle; Baizhang Huaihai calls the unnamed worker's response to the meal drum 'Guanyin's gate into principle'; Zhuanyu Guanheng asks where Guanyin is now; Zhongfeng Mingben says that with each raised thought one Guanyin appears; Linji Yixuan asks where twelve-faced Guanyin has gone; and Guizong Zhichang answers with a Guanyin formula before striking a cauldron lid.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Guanyin's gate of entry into principle
AlternateTargets: hearing as an entrance into realization

Occurrences.Kwic: 不久留汝等珍重。示眾師云今朝臘月十五夜半椎鐘擂鼓觀音入理之門到此休教莽鹵不莽鹵五九四十五五九四十五窮漢街頭舞
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (L/L154/L154n1639.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Tianyin Xiu (天隱修禪師語錄). Speaker: Tianyin Yuanxiu.

Occurrences.Kwic: 輝天。花簇簇、錦簇簇，一本同條，聯葩並馥。耳順啟觀音入理之門，從心處普賢歸源之府。黃金奕葉劫前香，碧玉迴環言
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J34/J34nB301.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Jiqi of Nanyue (南嶽繼起和尚語錄). Speaker: Jiqi Hongchu.

Occurrences.Kwic: 剃，上堂。學人問：「十方俱擊鼓，十處一齊聞，端的觀音入理之門，因甚王老師不打？」師云：「若將耳聽終難會。」宗

Occurrences.Kwic: 一僧聞鼓鳴，舉起鋤頭，大笑便歸。丈云：俊哉！此是觀音入理之門。丈歸，乃喚其僧問：適來汝見什麼道理便恁麼？僧云
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1411.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Hengchuan Xinggong (橫川行珙禪師語錄). Speaker: Baizhang Huaihai. Outer frame actor: Hengchuan Rugong serves as later-raiser.

Senses.Explanation: Guanyin's gate of entering principle is named beside midnight bells and drums, hearing, a questioned drum-strike, and Baizhang's meal-drum case. A demonstration joins midnight bell and drum to Guanyin's gate; a birthday address links mature hearing to it; the named student asks why the Miaozhan respondent does not strike the drum; Baizhang identifies the field-working monk's response to the meal drum as the gate.
